newsitem.title: ITALY: Zaire welcomes reports of Rwanda refugee return.
newsitem.headline: Zaire welcomes reports of Rwanda refugee return.

text.p: A Zairean minister said on Friday he hoped evidence that thousands of Hutu refugees were heading back to Rwanda marked the beginning of a mass return.

"I hope so with all my heart," Deputy Prime Minister Mutombo Bakafwa Nsenda told reporters when asked whether the fact that thousands of Hutu refugees had abandoned camps in eastern Zaire and were heading for the border signalled a large-scale exodus.
The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees earlier reported from Geneva that 10,000 Rwandan Hutus had crossed the border from Goma in eastern Zaire, where they had been put at risk from fighting.

Spokesman Fernando del Mundo told Reuters that by the end of Friday, 100,000 Rwandan Hutus could be on the Rwandan side of the border near Gisenyi town, Rwanda's northwestern border crossing with Zaire.

"The citizens that you're so worried about have their countries and their own governments," Mutombo said. Zaire has pressed for the refugees from Rwanda and Burundi to return home and said aid should be sent to their countries of origin.
"The problem of refugees is a problem for the Rwandans amongst themselves," Mutombo said. "I can't be moved that the refugees are going home -- whatever could be more natural."
